> Curated Travel Magazine https://www.curatedtravelmagazine.com/ Travel reporting, cultural heritage, and responsible exploration worldwide. en-US http://www.curatedtravelmagazine.com/assets/images/logo.png Sonoma County’s Culinary Scene Reaches New Heights With Three Michelin Stars for Enclos https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-countys-culinary-scene-reaches https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-countys-culinary-scene-reaches Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 18:09:04 GMT

Sonoma County has added another major distinction to its culinary reputation. Enclos Sonoma has risen from two Michelin stars to three in the 2026 Michelin Guide, placing the restaurant among the guide’s highest-rated destinations only months after making its debut with two stars in 2025.

The latest awards also brought a first Michelin star to Troubadour, while SingleThread retained its three-star designation and Green Star for its environmental sustainability and stewardship. Cyrus maintained its one-star rating. Beyond the starred restaurants, six Sonoma County establishments earned Bib Gourmand recognition for high-quality cooking at more accessible prices: El Molino Central, Valley Bar + Bottle, Glen Ellen Star, Khom Loi, Ramen Gaijin and Stockhome.

The Curated Take: Three Michelin stars is news anywhere, but Enclos’ trajectory makes the recognition particularly striking. Sonoma County’s culinary reputation is no longer simply an extension of its wine culture. The county has developed a dining ecosystem capable of supporting everything from highly ambitious tasting menus to neighborhood restaurants recognized for value, giving travelers another reason to plan an entire trip around the table.

Sonoma’s Wine Country Is Changing the Way Travelers Taste https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonomas-wine-country-is-changing https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonomas-wine-country-is-changing Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:35:11 GMT

Wine tasting in Sonoma County is becoming less about standing at a tasting bar and more about experiencing the landscape, history and people behind the bottle.

Marimar Estate Vineyards & Winery is celebrating its 40th anniversary in Sonoma County this year, marking four decades since Marimar Torres planted Chardonnay at Don Miguel Vineyard in the Green Valley of the Russian River Valley. Today, the family-owned estate farms 70 acres across the Russian River Valley and West Sonoma Coast, producing cool-climate wines including Chardonnay and Pinot Noir while continuing its focus on sustainability and multigenerational stewardship.

Elsewhere, Stone Edge Farm Estate Vineyards & Winery has opened La Maison, its first public tasting room after more than two decades of producing limited-production estate wines. The appointment-only experience brings together Moon Mountain District wines, regenerative agriculture, gardens and residential-style hospitality. The relationship extends to nearby Enclos, Chef Brian Limoges’ newly three-Michelin-starred restaurant, with an Enclos Lounge experience pairing Stone Edge Farm wines with small plates. At the Russian River estuary, Siren’s Cellar offers another distinctly different experience: a relaxed coastal wine bar overseen by sommelier and Monte Rio Cellars winemaker Patrick Cappiello, featuring natural wines, small producers and regional food.

The Curated Take: Sonoma’s newest wine experiences are increasingly about context. A bottle becomes more memorable when you understand the vineyard, the farm, the coastline or the chef connected to it. That shift makes Wine Country feel less like a series of tasting appointments and more like a destination where agriculture, hospitality and cuisine are part of the same story.

Photo credit: Marimar Estate

Sonoma County Makes Getting There Easier, From Austin and Denver to the Airport Parking Lot https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-county-makes-getting-there https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/sonoma-county-makes-getting-there Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:25:57 GMT

Sonoma County is making the journey into Wine Country a little easier. Southwest Airlines will launch seasonal Saturday nonstop service between Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport and Austin-Bergstrom International Airport on October 3, 2026, giving Central Texas travelers a direct route to Sonoma’s vineyards, redwood forests, Sonoma Coast and small towns.

The airline is also expanding its Denver service, moving to daily nonstop flights beginning March 11, 2027, after ramping up service during the fall, Thanksgiving and winter holiday periods. Meanwhile, travelers arriving at the airport will find a decidedly more modern experience on the ground. Charles M. Schulz Sonoma County Airport has introduced California’s first Metropolis drive-in, drive-out airport parking system, allowing registered travelers to enter and exit without tickets or payment kiosks. Vehicle recognition handles payment automatically, with digital receipts sent after the trip.

The Curated Take: Air access rarely feels like a travel story until it changes the way a destination can be reached. Sonoma County’s expanding connections to Austin and Denver do exactly that, opening the region to new drive-free itineraries while making the airport experience itself more seamless. For travelers accustomed to flying into larger Bay Area airports and driving north, STS increasingly makes the case for starting the Wine Country experience closer to the vineyards.

Island Hopper Brings Songwriters to the Water for 10 Days of Music https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/island-hopper-brings-songwriters https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/island-hopper-brings-songwriters Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:19:30 GMT

Southwest Florida’s Island Hopper Songwriter Fest returns September 18–27 with 10 days of intimate performances across Captiva Island, Cape Coral, downtown Fort Myers and Fort Myers Beach. Now in its 12th year, the festival brings more than 80 performances from acclaimed singer-songwriters to a distinctly tropical setting, with most shows free to attend. For those looking for a closer connection to the music, a limited selection of ticketed experiences pairs live performances with some decidedly memorable Southwest Florida settings.

This year’s special events include “Stars on the River,” featuring LOCASH and Alexandra Kay at Caloosa Sound Amphitheater; a Sunday brunch on Captiva with Dylan Altman and Tim James; Edwin McCain’s Westin Unplugged performance in Cape Coral; songwriter dinners in Cape Coral and downtown Fort Myers; and a sunset songwriter cruise departing Fort Myers Beach. The festival closes September 27 with Michael Ray performing a pool-party finale at Pink Shell Beach Resort & Marina, giving music lovers plenty of ways to build an entire getaway around the festival.

The Curated Take:
The best music festivals don’t simply give you a lineup; they give you a sense of place. Island Hopper does exactly that, turning beaches, waterways, restaurants, resorts and historic venues into part of the experience. A sunset cruise with a songwriter or live music overlooking the Gulf feels very different from sitting in a conventional concert hall, and that combination of intimate performances and tropical scenery makes this one worth planning a trip around.

Photo credit: Fort Myers – Islands, Beaches and Neighborhoods / Island Hopper Songwriter Fest

Branson’s Ozark Roads Become the Backdrop for the First National H.O.G. Rally https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/bransons-ozark-roads-become-the-backdrop https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/bransons-ozark-roads-become-the-backdrop Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:17:24 GMT

Motorcycle culture is rolling into Branson, Missouri, as the city hosts the inaugural National Harley Owners Group (H.O.G.) Rally September 10–12. Historic Downtown Branson will become the gathering point for riders from nearly 40 states, with a three-day lineup combining scenic motorcycle rides through the Ozark hills with live music, food, bike games, stunt performances and the unmistakable atmosphere of a major motorcycle rally. The events are free and open to the public, making this as much a Branson experience as a gathering for Harley enthusiasts.

The entertainment lineup ranges from an AC/DC tribute by Big Gun and country artist Demun Jones to Branson favorites The Petersens and national headliner Jackyl. Daily attractions include performances on the Wall of Death and other motorcycle stunts, while a special September 11 remembrance ceremony will honor 9/11 heroes and feature performances by veteran artists. Registered rally participants can also receive VIP concert access, exclusive merchandise and discounts at local attractions, giving riders plenty of reasons to extend their stay beyond the rally itself.

The Curated Take:
For motorcycle travelers, the destination is often just as important as the event, and Branson has an unusually good backdrop for a rally built around the open road. The Ozark hills provide the scenic riding, while Historic Downtown delivers the restaurants, shopping and entertainment that make it easy to turn a three-day event into a longer getaway. And because the rally is free to the public, even travelers who don’t arrive on a Harley can experience the spectacle and energy of a national motorcycle gathering.

Photo credit: Explore Branson / Branson Lakes Area Chamber of Commerce & CVB

Florida’s New Trail Towns Put Stuart and Port Salerno on the Outdoor Travel Map https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/floridas-new-trail-towns-put-stuart https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/floridas-new-trail-towns-put-stuart Sandra Thomas-Comenole Sun, 06 Sep 2026 14:12:05 GMT

Two Martin County communities are earning new recognition as gateways to Florida’s outdoors. Stuart and Port Salerno have been designated official Florida Trail Towns by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection’s Office of Greenways and Trails, joining a growing network of communities recognized for connecting long-distance, non-motorized trails with local businesses, natural areas and community experiences. For travelers who prefer their Florida escapes on two wheels, two feet or by paddle, the designation highlights a different side of the Sunshine State.

In Stuart, trail connections include the East Coast Greenway and Martin County Blueway Paddle Trail, while the Sailfish Healthy Trail and Stuart Riverwalk make it possible to combine outdoor exploration with downtown restaurants, shops, parks, public art and events. Port Salerno brings a waterfront perspective, connecting the East Coast Greenway and St. Lucie Blueway Paddle Trail with fishing culture, maritime history, restaurants, parks and protected natural areas. The designation follows a collaborative effort among county officials, tourism leaders, municipalities and local businesses to ensure trail users have the infrastructure and amenities to comfortably explore the area.

The Curated Take:
Florida’s outdoor appeal is often reduced to beaches, but Martin County makes a compelling case for looking inland and along the waterways. The Trail Town designation turns Stuart and Port Salerno into more than places you pass through on the way to the coast. They become bases for a slower kind of Florida adventure, where a morning ride or paddle can lead directly into a waterfront lunch, a stroll through town or an afternoon exploring local history. For travelers seeking soft adventure without sacrificing comfort and culture, that combination is worth knowing about.

Canberra Blooms, Glows and Comes Alive This Spring https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/canberra-blooms-glows-and-comes-alive https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/canberra-blooms-glows-and-comes-alive Sandra Thomas-Comenole Fri, 04 Sep 2026 13:44:42 GMT

Spring gives Canberra plenty of reasons to be on a traveler’s radar, from more than a million flowers transforming Commonwealth Park into a colorful spectacle to after-dark celebrations, immersive art, literary gatherings and creative festivals. Floriade, Australia’s largest celebration of spring, returns September 12 through October 11 for its 39th year, with this year’s Feast of Flowers theme adding seasonal food, edible gardens and shared experiences to the festival’s signature floral displays. Come October, NightFest takes the blooms into the evening with illuminated gardens, food and drink, and live music across four nights.

The city’s cultural calendar is equally compelling. At the Canberra Museum and Gallery, RELICS: A New World Rises transforms vintage objects into elaborate miniature worlds built entirely from LEGO® bricks, while the National Gallery of Australia presents monumental tapestries by Australian artist Arthur Boyd through October 18. October also brings the 10th anniversary of the Canberra Writers Festival, featuring more than 110 events and 200 writers, while November’s Craft + Design Canberra Festival explores creativity, dissent and social change through exhibitions, workshops, open studios, markets and public art. Together, the lineup makes Canberra particularly appealing for travelers looking for a spring city break with considerably more substance than sightseeing alone.

The Curated Take:
Canberra’s spring story is bigger than flowers, even if the flowers are spectacular. What makes this lineup particularly appealing is the way the city’s gardens, galleries, design scene, literature and live events overlap, creating a destination that rewards travelers who want to do something rather than simply see something. Add in the compact nature of the Australian capital, and a long weekend could easily become a cultural deep dive.

At Sunset, Guests Can Help a Baby Sea Turtle Find Its Way Home https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/at-sunset-guests-can-help-a-baby https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/at-sunset-guests-can-help-a-baby Sandra Thomas-Comenole Fri, 04 Sep 2026 12:17:08 GMT

For the first time, Atlantis Paradise Island is giving guests the chance to take part in one of nature’s most remarkable moments: the release of newly hatched green sea turtles into the Atlantic. Available through the end of September and timed around the natural hatching of the resort’s nests, the limited-time Baby Sea Turtle Release offers travelers a rare opportunity to witness a hatchling’s first journey into the wild.

The experience begins with a visit to The Royal Fish Hospital, where guests learn about green sea turtles, their habitat and the conservation work helping protect them. At sunset, the educational experience becomes hands-on as each participant releases a baby turtle into the ocean, guiding it along Atlantis’ designated “Sea Turtle Highway.” The program is open to guests age six and older, with reservations required and availability dependent on when the nests hatch.

The Curated Take:
There are wildlife experiences, and then there are moments that make you stop and realize you are witnessing the very beginning of a life. The appeal here isn’t simply getting close to sea turtles; it’s the combination of education, conservation and participation, culminating at sunset with a tiny hatchling making its first push toward the sea. For families visiting the Bahamas, it’s the kind of experience that can turn a resort stay into a story everyone remembers long after the vacation is over.

Photo credit: Atlantis Paradise Island

When Thai Heritage Becomes Something You Can Take Home https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/when-thai-heritage-becomes-something https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/when-thai-heritage-becomes-something Sandra Thomas-Comenole Fri, 04 Sep 2026 12:10:11 GMT

A new collaboration between Anantara Hotels & Resorts and Thai heritage silk house Jim Thompson brings the spirit of Thailand beyond the walls of the resort with Soul of Siam, an exclusive nine-piece collection of resort wear and travel accessories. Debuting September 1 across Anantara properties throughout Thailand, the collection translates the visual language of Thai culture into pieces designed to travel: a wrap kaftan, silk scarf, pocket square, beach bag, cap, vanity pouch and laptop cases, all featuring either the signature Soul of Siam print or a more understated deep navy palette.

The collection draws on imagery inspired by Thai temple architecture, mythical guardians, rural landscapes and tropical flora, while traditional silk-making techniques championed by Jim Thompson give the pieces a tangible connection to the country’s craft heritage. The collaboration builds on an existing relationship between the brands, including Jim Thompson-designed spaces at Anantara Siam Bangkok Hotel and Anantara Mai Khao Phuket Villas. Campaign imagery, photographed at Anantara Siam Bangkok and Anantara Riverside Bangkok, features Thai personalities Cindy Sirinya Bishop and Byron Bishop, adding a distinctly local face to the pairing of heritage and contemporary luxury.

The Curated Take:
The most interesting luxury souvenirs are the ones that don’t look like souvenirs. Soul of Siam takes something deeply rooted in Thai culture and turns it into something travelers can actually incorporate into their lives long after the resort stay ends. It also reflects a broader evolution in luxury hospitality, where the experience increasingly extends beyond the room itself and into design, fashion and objects with a sense of place. For travelers who want to bring a piece of Thailand home without resorting to the predictable, this collaboration makes the destination wearable.

Vienna at Christmas, on Her Own Terms https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/vienna-at-christmas-on-her-own-terms https://curatedtravelmagazine.substack.com/p/vienna-at-christmas-on-her-own-terms Sandra Thomas-Comenole Fri, 04 Sep 2026 12:07:44 GMT

What if the European Christmas trip you’ve always dreamed about didn’t have to wait for someone else’s calendar? That’s the idea behind Illuminare Retreat, where founder Amanda Donaho is seeing more women choose meaningful travel on their own rather than postpone it until a partner, friend or family member is available. Her intimate European retreats offer a middle ground between traditional group travel and going completely solo, giving women the freedom to travel independently with the ease, connection and thoughtful planning of a curated experience.

That approach takes on a particularly festive dimension this year with Illuminare’s inaugural Vienna Christmas Retreat, a week designed around the Austrian capital’s Christmas markets, historic cafés, cultural experiences and holiday traditions. The retreat speaks to a broader shift in how women are approaching solo travel, particularly among women in their 30s through 70s who are looking not only for independence, but also friendship, discovery and the opportunity to experience a destination on their own terms.

The Curated Take:
There’s something wonderfully liberating about refusing to put a dream trip on hold simply because the right travel companion hasn’t appeared on the calendar. Vienna at Christmas is already a compelling proposition, but the more interesting story here is the growing confidence behind women traveling independently while still wanting the social connection of a shared experience. Solo doesn’t have to mean solitary, and for travelers who have spent years coordinating everyone else’s schedules, that may be the most appealing luxury of all.
